title: Ashaveri Evidence Pack (JSON twin of the CBOR/COSE container)
description: Display-only projection of the signed COSE_Sign1 pack container. The CBOR bytes are canonical; this JSON form is never signed directly. Byte strings appear as lowercase hex, which is how the receipt's own projection writes them, and a length that is a number of bytes in the CBOR is not the same measure as a JSON string length, so only `minLength` on an id carries a bound the framing states and nothing else here pretends to. Closure is not the manifest's alone: the manifest map and every map it opens, `span`, `chain`, `duty`, each entry of `items` and each entry of `carried`, name their members in the same object, which is where `additionalProperties` applies, so a member the format does not define is refused at that level rather than read and dropped on the way to a verifier. `protectedHeader` carries the three labels the CDDL declares and no more, and this definition carries no closure keyword: that map is read by number, its bytes are what the signature hashes, and a document carrying a fourth label is refused before any projection of it is built. The envelope above it is projected more loosely than the format writes it, and that is a decision rather than a gap: this document requires `protectedHeader` and `payload`, names `signature` without demanding it, and leaves its own root unclosed, so a pack shown before it is signed still shows, while `pack.cddl` requires all four elements of the `COSE_Sign1` and sixty-four bytes in the fourth of them. Requiring the missing one here would refuse a display and not an artifact, which is the same reason the receipt's projection is written the same way. The CBOR tag that wraps the four elements on the wire, tag 18, is stated in `pack.cddl` and cannot be stated here at all, because a JSON object has no tag to carry: a reader who needs the bytes needs the format, and that is where the number is. `art` is not an enum here because the retention-duty registry is a reader's question rather than this file's, which is also why the CDDL writes it `tstr`: a label the reader cannot interpret is refused by the reader that knows the registry, and a format that listed the labels it happens to know would decide a legal question it cannot check. No member states whether the duty was met, and that is the format's decision rather than an omission: a reader holding `at`, `held` and `required` answers it in one comparison, and a conclusion the deployment signed about itself is worth less as evidence than the three integers are. The rules that hold between two members are not spelled out here because no keyword reaches them: that every item's stamp lies inside the span, that the end of the span is no later than the instant assembly began, that the revision the period came from precedes it, that the seconds held are at least the age of the oldest receipt in this pack, that no two items answer to one `id`, that every item of the array is reached from the anchor, that every entry of `carried` states the digest its own bytes hash to and no digest is stated twice, that every entry is named by a slot of some sealed receipt and every slot that states material is answered by an entry, and that the list and each entry of it lie under the two ceilings the format takes from its own contents, and that no instant lies before the epoch and no duration below zero, are all stated in `pack.cddl`, which is where a reader holding this projection has to go to learn them. Nothing in this repository decides what a pack is assembled from, and `packages/receipt/src/pack.ts` both writes these bytes and reads them back, so this definition and `pack.cddl` are the layout that writer is held to and the one a second implementation can be measured against.

kid.description: sha256 of the Ed25519 public key, hex

typ.description: the content type that tells a pack apart from a receipt, which the same key signs

payload.description: The signed manifest, and the only part of a pack a verifier has to believe before it starts walking. Exactly one version is defined, so `v` is a constant rather than a discriminant, and a document naming another version is not this one.

signature.description: Ed25519 signature over the Sig_structure, hex

at.description: unix seconds, the instant assembly began, stamped before the reads so a slow store cannot date a pack later than the window it describes

span.description: the period the pack answers for, half-open: `from` included, `to` excluded

chain.description: the two endpoints a reader walks between, neither of them derivable from the items

duty.description: the retention duty the pack answers, and the revision of the mapping the required period was read from

items.description: The receipts, at least one. Order in this array carries nothing: a reader follows each item's `prev` to find its predecessor, because retiring a prefix rewrites the front of a chain without touching a surviving record's digest, and the item whose `prev` is the anchor is first while the one whose own digest is the head is last. A pack of nothing would have no first item, so its walk would be vacuous, which is why `minItems` is one and not a courtesy.

carried.description: The material the two slots of a sealed receipt's `cva` name, carried inside the container that seals the receipt naming them, so a reader holding this file and nothing else can weigh a slot. It may be empty, and an empty list is the pack saying it carries nothing rather than the pack failing to say: every sealed receipt states an anchor with both of its halves, so the pack that writes this member empty is the one whose every slot states an absence. Resolution is by content hash and by nothing else, because the digest a slot states is the only name needed, and the pack does not key an entry to a receipt the issuer chose. The list is a list rather than a map for that reason and one more: deduplication lives inside it, so one object appears once however many sealed receipts name it, and a second name for one thing is the thing that drifts. `minItems` is absent because emptiness is a lawful statement, and the two ceilings this member carries, an entry's byte count and the count of entries against the two slots per item, are stated in `pack.cddl` because no keyword here reaches either side of a length.

manifest.description: A pack manifest and nothing else. The map is closed: a member outside this list is a malformed pack rather than a member a reader agreed to forget, and the same holds of every map below it.

to.description: unix seconds, excluded: a receipt issued at exactly this stamp belongs to the next pack

span.description: The half-open interval the store served, which is the bound the store's own range query uses. The walk shows that nothing between the first item and the last is missing; this is what shows a reader whether the run they are reading is the period they asked for.

anchor.description: the digest the first item was chained from: thirty-two zero bytes before any retirement, otherwise the seam a trim record carried

head.description: the digest of the last item in the chain

chain.description: Both endpoints inside the signature, which is what gives the walk its meaning. An anchor a reader invented would let a deployment start the walk wherever it liked and a head read off the last item handed over would let it stop there, so a run of receipts the reader was never shown would go unseen. Publishing the head is what makes deletion detectable.

art.description: a label from the retention-duty registry, which this estate reads as "19(1)", "19(2)" and "26(6)". Not an enum here because the CDDL admits any tstr: the reader that knows the registry refuses a label outside it, and 19(2) and 26(6) route a financial institution's logs into applicable Union financial-services law, which this format does not interpret.

rev.description: unix seconds, the revision of the mapping `required` was read from. The member that makes the other three readable later: a claim made in 2027 is read against the revision it was made from, not against whatever the mapping says the day the artifact is opened.

required.description: seconds that revision of the mapping required, which is the deployment's to state and this format supplies no default for

held.description: seconds the store has held the oldest receipt it still retains, measured at `at`. Not derivable from the items, which is the only reason it is stated: a pack covers one span and the duty runs against everything retained.

duty.description: The duty, the period, the revision the period came from, and the time actually held. Whether the duty was met is absent on purpose: a reader comparing `held` with `required` answers it, and an artifact that states the conclusion beside the evidence invites a reader to stop checking the numbers.

id.description: the store's own id for the receipt, as the record names it. The framing bounds it at 65535 bytes and an empty id belongs to a trim record, which is never an item; `minLength` is the half of that a JSON length can state, and the CBOR is where the byte bound is read.

iat.description: unix seconds, the stamp the record was chained at. It has to equal the `iat` the receipt itself attests: the store chains a receipt under the stamp it was handed, so a reader who checked the walk and not this equality would accept a receipt moved into a window it was never issued in.

prev.description: the digest of the record before this one, or the anchor for the first item

receipt.description: the signed receipt bytes, whole and unaltered, exactly as the record's payload holds them. Each entry verifies on its own as `receipt-v1.schema.json` describes it, and this container adds nothing to what a receipt attests.

item.description: One receipt with the three values its record was hashed with, which is all it takes to rebuild that record's frame: the kind byte is 0 for every item, the id length and the record length count bytes that follow them, and the digest the next item names is sha256 over the kind, the predecessor digest, `iat` as eight big-endian bytes, the id length as two big-endian bytes, the id and the receipt bytes.

bytes.description: The material exactly as it arrived, and the whole of it: signed collateral, a validity window's material, revocation data. The CBOR bounds this run of bytes at 65535, which is the largest byte count the container already states, the one `id` is bounded at because the framing spends two bytes on its length; a JSON string length cannot state a byte bound, so the ceiling lives in `pack.cddl` and this projection names no number for it.

sha256.description: sha256 of the bytes beside it. The reader recomputes it and refuses a disagreement, which is what makes the entry a statement about its own bytes rather than a label over bytes the reader cannot see; a digest that does not match is a malformed pack, not a hint about which of the two the issuer meant.

carried.description: One object the pack carries, stated as its bytes and as the digest of those bytes. A projection can show both and can check neither against the other, and it does not pretend to: resolution, the refusal of a stated digest that disagrees with its bytes, the refusal of a digest carried twice, the refusal of an entry no sealed slot names and the refusal of a slot whose material the pack does not carry are all stated in `pack.cddl` and enforced by the reader that recomputes them.
